```{r setup}
library(BsplineQuantReg)
```

The R-packege "Quantile regression with B-splines under shape constraints" is intended to perform quantile regression with polynomial splines. It follows the method described in Abbes(2025) <doi:10.5281/zenodo.17427913>, and initiated by He and Shi (1998) for quadratic splines, on the original idea of Koenker and Basset for linear regression.

## Simple example

``` {r simple example, fig.width=10, fig.height=7, out.width="100%"}


 n_points <- 50
  xtab = ((0:(n_points)) / (n_points))

  # simple pscillating data
  #ytab<- -3 * xtab +sin(3*2*xtab*3.14)+ 0.2 * rnorm(n_points+1)
  #ytab= <- 2* xtab + 0.5 * sin(6 * pi * xtab) + 0.1 * rnorm(n_points+1)
  ytab <- xtab * (1 - xtab) + 0.1 * rnorm(n_points + 1)
  kn <- 8

  n = 7

  monot1 = c(rep(1, n), rep(0, (12 - n)))
  monot2 = rep(1,12)
  knot <- ((0:(kn + 5)) / (kn + 5))
  
  res <- quantile_spline(
    xtab = xtab,
    ytab = ytab,
    knot,
    tau = 0.5,
    monot = 0,
    degree = 3,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
 res_part_croissant <- quantile_spline(
    xtab = xtab,
    ytab = ytab,
    knot = knot,
    tau = 0.5,
    degree = 3,
    monot = monot1,
    convcons = 0,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
 
 res_croissant <- quantile_spline(
    xtab = xtab,
    ytab = ytab,
    knot = knot,
    tau = 0.5,
    degree = 3,
    monot = 1,
    convcons = 0,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
 
 
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
x_eval=(0:200)/200
  y_sans = spline_eval(res, x_eval)
  y_part_croiss = spline_eval(res_part_croissant, x_eval)
  y_croiss = spline_eval(res_croissant, x_eval)
  
    plot(
    xtab,
    ytab,
    pch = 16,
    cex = 0.5,
    col = "black",
    main = c("Without constraint")
    )
    lines(x_eval, y_sans, lwd = 2)  
    
  plot(
    xtab,
    ytab,
    pch = 16,
    cex = 0.5,
    col = "black",
    main = c("Mixed mootone :\n global increasing constraints
                "
    )
  )
  lines(x_eval, y_croiss, lwd = 2)  

    
    plot(
    xtab,
    ytab,
    pch = 16,
    cex = 0.5,
    col = "black",
    main = c("Mixed mootone :\n increasing constraints
                \n on the first inter-knots"
    )
  )
  lines(x_eval, y_part_croiss, lwd = 2)  


```

## Content

***The initial version with cubic splines*** is now augmented with splines of degree 0 to 4 for constrained regression, and any degree for regression without monotone constraints. 

**see the demo** *degrees_comparison*    Simultaneous comparison of constraints across degrees 1, 2, 3, and 4

***Constraints for degrees 3*** (monotone), degree 4 (monotone and convex) and 5 (convex) use the Karlin-Studden SOCP characterization.

**see the vignette** *theoretical_background* and *shape_constraints*.

**see the demos**:
-*monotonicity_basic*    Monotonicity constraints demo.
-*convexity*             Convexity and concavity constraints demo.
-*temperature*           Temperature anomaly analysis: uniform increasing vs mixed constraints (decreasing 1956-1973 only).
-*temperature2*          Temperature anomaly analysis with alternative constraint configurations.
-*logistic*              Quantile regression test on a logistic function.
-*comprehensive*         Comprehensive test of various constraints on an oscillating function.

***It can handle third derivatives constraints*** for the degrees 3 and 4.

**see the demo**: *demo_der3* (Demonstration of third-order derivative constraints)



***All B-spline and polynomial functions*** have been rewritten for consistency. This package provides an original B-spline library for conversion between PP-form and B-spline
    representation, evaluation, differentiation, callable and
    non-callable objects, print human readable pp forms, view basis,
    all based on "De Boor\'s" theory. 
    
**See the corresponding vignettes** : *polynomial_library* and *bspline_basis_manipulation*.

Differentiation of Bsplines can be operated on the spline (polynomial differentiation) or on the basis.

**see the demo** *derivative2*  (Demonstration for the coherence of the derivative functions.)

***It also extends to multiple knots*** to catch up singularities. This feature is robust in the package including for constrained regression.
  
** See the demos **   *shock*     (Regression with Discontinuity and Derivability Singularity) and  *shock_basis*  (same as shock, with singular B-spline basis display).
    


    
## Graphical user interface

An interactive Shiny GUI is available at
https://cran.r-project.org/package=BsplineQuantRegGui
and <https://github.com/<user>/BsplineQuantRegGUI>:
```{r gui}
# install.packages("BsplineQuantRegGui")
#or 
# install.packages("remotes")
#remotes::install_github("<user>/BsplineQuantRegGUI")
#BsplineQuantRegGUI::run_app()
```

The GUI lets you create a custom data set, upload a two-column dataset, choose the spline degree, knots, quantile level, and shape constraints (monotone, convex, …), and
download the fitted curve and coefficients, with an executable R code.


## An equivalent Python package is available
    at <https://pypi.org/project/BsplineQuantRegpy/>.
